guide.title: Union Square, San Francisco: the plaza, Maiden Lane and the north side of Market Street
guide.intro: Union Square is the retail core of downtown San Francisco, and the square it is named for is a city plaza at 333 Post Street, bounded by Geary, Powell, Post and Stockton Streets. San Francisco Recreation and Parks records it as a civic plaza of 2.6 acres. The Dewey Monument stands at its centre and four steel columns stand along its south side. Powell Street runs from the plaza down to Market Street, where the Powell-Hyde and Powell-Mason cable car lines are turned by hand on a turntable. Maiden Lane runs east from Stockton Street to Kearny Street, past the V. C. Morris Building. Post, Sutter, Geary and Grant carry the shops. The north side of Market Street carries the Flood, Phelan, Chronicle and Wells Fargo buildings, and the theatres stand on the Geary Street block at 415 and 445.

sections.heading: The square, Maiden Lane and the Geary Street theatres
sections.body:
The plaza is at 333 Post Street, bounded by Geary, Powell, Post and Stockton Streets, and San Francisco Recreation and Parks records it as a civic plaza of 2.6 acres owned by the department. No source states opening hours for it, so none are given here. The Dewey Monument is a bronze figure on a granite column at the centre of the plaza, by Robert Ingersoll Aitken; the San Francisco Arts Commission dates it to 1901 and gives its height as 1,265 inches, which is 105 feet 5 inches. Four columns by R. M. Fischer stand on the south side of the plaza, in stainless steel, polycarbonate and aluminium on granite, and the Arts Commission dates them to about 1999-2002, giving two at 240 inches high and two at 180. The Union Square Garage is beneath the plaza at the same address, telephone 415.765.9069, open Monday to Sunday from 5:00am to 11:00pm and run by LAZ Parking from January 2018.

The Westin St. Francis is at 335 Powell Street, facing the plaza. Beacon Grand is at 450 Powell Street in a building of 1930, and its Starlite Room bar is on the twenty-first floor. The Chancellor Hotel is at 433 Powell Street, in a building of 1914. Sears Fine Food is at 439 Powell Street, open every day from 7am to 3pm and again from 5pm to 9pm, with its Swedish pancakes served eighteen to an order.

Maiden Lane runs between Stockton Street and Kearny Street. It is a street: no operator, no admission and no hours. San Francisco Planning's parcel records give construction years along it - number 16 in 1906; 34-40, 50-58 and 60 in 1908; 177 in 1907; 140 and 170 in 1909; 134 in 1910; 69 in 1920; and 118-120 in 2001. The V. C. Morris Building at 140 Maiden Lane is San Francisco Landmark No. 72, designated in 1975, and San Francisco Planning records its shell as built in 1909.

Three venues stand on the Geary Street block. The Toni Rembe Theater is at 415 Geary Street: the building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 27 May 1975 as the Geary Theatre, reference number 75000472, and San Francisco designated it Landmark No. 82 the following year, in 1976. The Curran Theatre is at 445 Geary Street, in a building SF Planning records as built in 1922, and is programmed by BroadwaySF. The Clift Royal Sonesta San Francisco is at 495 Geary Street, and its bars and dining rooms include the Redwood Room, Fredericks and The Living Room. August Hall is at 420 Mason Street, with a kitchen called Fifth Arrow and Gold Leaf Catering in the same building.

sections.heading: Market Street's north side, Grant Avenue and Bush Street
sections.body:
The north side of Market Street between Fifth Street and Kearny Street carries a run of buildings that each hold a register citation. The James Flood Building at 870-898 Market Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 154, designated in 1982, in a building of 1907. Samuel's Clock is a street clock on the pavement at 856 Market Street: San Francisco Landmark No. 77, designated in 1975. The Phelan Building at 760-784 Market Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 156, designated in 1982, in a building of 1908. The Wells Fargo Union Trust Branch at 744 Market Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 131, designated in 1981, in a building of 1910. The Chronicle Building at 690 Market Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 243, designated in 2007. At the corner of Grant Avenue and Market Street, the Savings Union Bank branch at 1 Grant Avenue is San Francisco Landmark No. 132, designated in 1981.

The Golden Triangle Light Standards are the cast street light standards of the retail blocks between Market and Sutter Streets. They are San Francisco Landmark No. 233, designated in 2003, and they run through the whole of the shopping core rather than standing on any one parcel.

Grant Avenue carries the Home Telephone Company Building at 333 Grant Avenue, San Francisco Landmark No. 141, designated in 1981. Sutter Street carries the Hammersmith Building at 303 Sutter Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 117, designated in 1980, and the Four Fifty Sutter Building at 450 Sutter Street, listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 22 December 2009, reference number 09001118. The Metropolitan Club at 640 Sutter Street was listed on the National Register on 10 September 2004 as the Woman's Athletic Club of San Francisco, reference number 04000955. The City of Paris Building at 181-199 Geary Street was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 23 January 1975, reference number 75000471, and Neiman Marcus takes addresses at 150 Stockton Street and 199 Geary Street.

On Bush Street, Notre Dame des Victoires Church and Rectory at 564-566 Bush Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 173, designated in 1984, and Fire Station 2 at 460 Bush Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 143, designated in 1981, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 17 April 2002 as San Francisco Fire Department Engine Co. Number 2, reference number 02000371. At 600 Stockton Street, the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company's Pacific Coast head office building is San Francisco Landmark No. 167, designated in 1984. First Congregational Church at 432 Mason Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 177, designated in 1985.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Steer by the cable car turntable and by addresses. The Powell-Hyde and Powell-Mason cable car lines both begin at Powell and Market Streets, where the cars are turned by hand on a turntable. Fares at this stop must be bought before boarding between 8am and 8pm. The cable cars were listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 15 October 1966, reference number 66000233, and are a National Historic Landmark; the San Francisco Cable Car Historic District carries a period of significance beginning in 1873.

Two public garages serve the blocks around the square. The Sutter-Stockton Garage is at 444 Stockton Street and the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency gives it as always open, with bicycle parking. The Ellis-O'Farrell Garage is at 123 O'Farrell Street and opens Monday to Sunday from 6:00 am to 10:00 pm, also with bicycle parking. The Union Square Garage is beneath the plaza itself at 333 Post Street, open Monday to Sunday from 5:00am to 11:00pm.

The addresses that matter: Union Square, 333 Post Street, bounded by Geary, Powell, Post and Stockton. Maiden Lane, between Stockton Street and Kearny Street. The Toni Rembe Theater, 415 Geary Street; the Curran Theatre, 445 Geary Street. Britex Fabrics, 117 Post Street. Apple Union Square, 300 Post Street. Macy's Union Square, 170 O'Farrell Street. Sears Fine Food, 439 Powell Street. John's Grill, 63 Ellis Street.

faq.question: Where is Union Square itself, and is there anything in it?
faq.answer: The plaza is at 333 Post Street, bounded by Geary, Powell, Post and Stockton Streets. San Francisco Recreation and Parks records it as a civic plaza of 2.6 acres owned by the department, and no source states opening hours for it, so none are given here. The Dewey Monument stands at the centre: a bronze figure on a granite column by Robert Ingersoll Aitken, which the San Francisco Arts Commission dates to 1901 and gives as 1,265 inches high, or 105 feet 5 inches. Four columns by R. M. Fischer stand on the south side, in stainless steel, polycarbonate and aluminium on granite; the Arts Commission dates them to about 1999-2002 and gives two at 240 inches high and two at 180. The Union Square Garage is beneath the plaza at the same address, open Monday to Sunday from 5:00am to 11:00pm.

faq.question: Which buildings here carry a register citation?
faq.answer: On the Article 10 register: the V. C. Morris Building, 140 Maiden Lane, San Francisco Landmark No. 72, designated in 1975; the Hammersmith Building, 303 Sutter Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 117, designated in 1980; the James Flood Building, 870-898 Market Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 154, designated in 1982; Samuel's Clock, 856 Market Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 77, designated in 1975; the Phelan Building, 760-784 Market Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 156, designated in 1982; the Wells Fargo Union Trust Branch, 744 Market Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 131, designated in 1981; the Chronicle Building, 690 Market Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 243, designated in 2007; the Savings Union Bank branch, 1 Grant Avenue, San Francisco Landmark No. 132, designated in 1981; the Home Telephone Company Building, 333 Grant Avenue, San Francisco Landmark No. 141, designated in 1981; the Golden Triangle Light Standards, San Francisco Landmark No. 233, designated in 2003; First Congregational Church, 432 Mason Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 177, designated in 1985; Notre Dame des Victoires Church and Rectory, 564-566 Bush Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 173, designated in 1984; Fire Station 2, 460 Bush Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 143, designated in 1981; and the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company's Pacific Coast head office at 600 Stockton Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 167, designated in 1984. On the federal register: the Toni Rembe Theater at 415 Geary Street, listed on 27 May 1975 as the Geary Theatre, reference number 75000472; the Four Fifty Sutter Building, listed on 22 December 2009, reference number 09001118; the Metropolitan Club at 640 Sutter Street, listed on 10 September 2004, reference number 04000955; the City of Paris Building at 181-199 Geary Street, listed on 23 January 1975, reference number 75000471; and Fire Station 2, listed on 17 April 2002, reference number 02000371.

faq.question: Which shops around the square publish their opening hours?
faq.answer: Britex Fabrics at 117 Post Street opens Monday to Friday from 11am to 4pm and on the first Saturday of each month from 11am to 4pm; its button wall carries 75,000 styles and the telephone number is (415) 392-2910. Apple Union Square at 300 Post Street opens 10am to 8pm Monday to Saturday and 11am to 7pm on Sunday, with free Today at Apple sessions bookable online. Gump's at 250 Post Street, Tiffany & Co at 350 Post Street, Neiman Marcus at 150 Stockton Street and Macy's Union Square at 170 O'Farrell Street state no opening hours on any source, so none are given here.

faq.question: What is playing on the Geary Street theatre block?
faq.answer: The Toni Rembe Theater is at 415 Geary Street and is one of two venues run by the American Conservatory Theater, the other being The Strand Theater at 1127 Market Street. The Curran Theatre is at 445 Geary Street, in a building SF Planning records as built in 1922, and is programmed by BroadwaySF. Neither publishes a durable programme, so no show is named here. August Hall is at 420 Mason Street, with a kitchen called Fifth Arrow and Gold Leaf Catering in the same building; the venue occupies the premises that traded as Ruby Skye until 2017. The Marines' Memorial Theatre, inside the club at 609 Sutter Street, seats 564.

faq.question: Where do the cable cars start?
faq.answer: The Powell-Hyde and Powell-Mason lines both begin at Powell and Market Streets, where the cars are turned by hand on a turntable. Fares at this stop must be bought before boarding between 8am and 8pm. The cable cars were listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 15 October 1966, reference number 66000233, and are a National Historic Landmark; the San Francisco Cable Car Historic District carries a period of significance beginning in 1873.

faq.question: Where can I eat around the square?
faq.answer: Sears Fine Food is at 439 Powell Street, open every day from 7am to 3pm and again from 5pm to 9pm; its Swedish pancakes are served eighteen to an order and the menu also carries omelets, eggs Florentine, grilled Angus steak, San Francisco cioppino and steamed mussels with garlic toast. John's Grill is at 63 Ellis Street and has live jazz nightly. Morton's The Steakhouse is at 400 Post Street, Alexander's Steakhouse at 165 O'Farrell Street and Kin Khao at 55 Cyril Magnin Street. Marines' Memorial Club & Hotel at 609 Sutter Street has a rooftop restaurant called Chesty's Bar & Grill, and non-members may use its dining rooms as guests.

links.note: Kearny Street runs between the two, with the Hallidie Building and the Mechanics' Institute on its east side.
Grant Avenue and Stockton Street run north from the shopping blocks into Chinatown.
Powell Street climbs north from the square, carrying the cable cars that turn at Market Street over the hill.
The south side of Market Street faces the Flood, Phelan, Wells Fargo and Chronicle buildings across the roadway.
